command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/cache
mkdir -p /tmp/cache
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).

echo "== staged bytes must match their pin =="
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: dataset.tar does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
tar -xf dataset.tar
NSEQ=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="n_sequences"{print $2}' expected.tsv)

# DIAGNOSTICS BEFORE THE RUN. pangolin bundles its designation data as the `pangolin-data`
# package, and whether a given build can call lineages entirely offline is a property of the
# image rather than something to assume. Print what it has before asking it to work, so a
# failure is diagnosable from this log alone.
echo "== what this pangolin build actually has =="
pangolin --version 2>&1 | head -3
pangolin --all-versions 2>&1 | head -12
python3 -c "
import importlib.util as u
for m in ('pangolin','pangolin_data','scorpio','constellations'):
    s=u.find_spec(m)
    print('module\t%-16s %s' % (m, 'present' if s else 'MISSING'))
" 2>&1

echo "== call the same 165 sequences, offline =="
# --skip-scorpio avoids the constellations lookup; --analysis-mode usher is the default and
# uses the protobuf tree shipped in pangolin-data.
pangolin dataset/sequences.fasta --outfile pangolin.csv --tempdir /tmp/pangotmp \
  --threads "$(nproc)" --skip-designation-cache > pango.log 2>&1
RC=$?
printf 'pangolin_rc\t%s\n' "$RC"
if [ "$RC" != "0" ]; then
  echo "---- pangolin log tail ----"; tail -40 pango.log
  echo "FAIL: pangolin exited $RC"; exit 1
fi
test -s pangolin.csv || { tail -20 pango.log; echo "FAIL: pangolin wrote no output"; exit 1; }
head -2 pangolin.csv | sed 's/^/  /'
PROWS=$(( $(wc -l < pangolin.csv) - 1 ))
printf 'pangolin_rows\t%s\n' "$PROWS"
test "$PROWS" = "$NSEQ" || { echo "FAIL: pangolin produced $PROWS rows for $NSEQ sequences"; exit 1; }

python3 -u - <<'PYEOF' 2>&1 | tee compare.log
import sys, csv, json

# ---- nextclade side (carried over from task 1) ----
nc = {}
with open("nc_calls.tsv") as fh:
    r = csv.DictReader(fh, delimiter="\t")
    for row in r:
        nc[row["seqName"]] = (row["nextclade_pango"] or "").strip()
print("nextclade_calls\t%d" % len(nc))

# ---- pangolin side ----
pg = {}
with open("pangolin.csv") as fh:
    r = csv.DictReader(fh)
    if "taxon" not in r.fieldnames or "lineage" not in r.fieldnames:
        sys.exit("FAIL: pangolin.csv lacks taxon/lineage (%s)" % r.fieldnames)
    for row in r:
        pg[row["taxon"]] = (row["lineage"] or "").strip()
print("pangolin_calls\t%d" % len(pg))

# Nextclade keys on the full FASTA header, pangolin truncates at the first whitespace. Join on
# the first token of each, which is the sequence ID both derive from -- comparing the raw keys
# would silently intersect to nothing.
def key(s):
    return s.split()[0] if s else s
nck = {key(k): v for k, v in nc.items()}
pgk = {key(k): v for k, v in pg.items()}
shared = sorted(set(nck) & set(pgk))
print("shared_sequences\t%d" % len(shared))
if len(shared) < 100:
    sys.exit("FAIL: only %d sequences shared between the two outputs; the join key is wrong"
             % len(shared))

UNASSIGNED = {"", "Unassigned", "None", "unclassified"}
both = [s for s in shared if nck[s] not in UNASSIGNED and pgk[s] not in UNASSIGNED]
print("both_assigned\t%d" % len(both))

exact = sum(1 for s in both if nck[s] == pgk[s])
print("exact_agreement\t%d" % exact)
print("exact_agreement_rate\t%.4f" % (exact / len(both)) if both else "exact_agreement_rate\tNA")

# TWO THINGS HAVE TO BE RESOLVED BEFORE THESE NAMES ARE COMPARABLE, and the first attempt at
# this recipe only handled one of them.
#
# 1. HIERARCHY. BA.2 and BA.2.3 are not a disagreement -- one is more specific.
# 2. ALIASES. Pango gives a lineage a NEW LETTER PREFIX once its dotted name grows too long,
#    so C.* IS B.1.1.1.*, BA.* is B.1.1.529.*, AY.* is B.1.617.2.*. Measured: the only two
#    "disagreements" in the first run were nextclade=B.1.1.1 against pangolin=C.27, which name
#    the SAME placement. A prefix test cannot see that, because the strings share no prefix --
#    so that was a limitation of the metric, not a difference between the tools.
#
# Both calls are therefore unaliased into the B/A root namespace first, using the authoritative
# alias table pinned from pango-designation v1.41.
with open("alias_key.json") as fh:
    ALIAS = json.load(fh)
print("alias_entries\t%d" % len(ALIAS))

def unalias(lin):
    if not lin or lin in UNASSIGNED:
        return lin
    parts = lin.split(".")
    v = ALIAS.get(parts[0])
    # Recombinant lineages (X*) map to a LIST of parents and have no single root form, so they
    # are left as-is rather than forced into one arbitrarily.
    if isinstance(v, str) and v:
        return ".".join([v] + parts[1:])
    return lin

def compatible(a, b):
    a, b = unalias(a), unalias(b)
    if a == b:
        return True
    pa, pb = a.split("."), b.split(".")
    n = min(len(pa), len(pb))
    return pa[:n] == pb[:n]
exact_un = sum(1 for s in both if unalias(nck[s]) == unalias(pgk[s]))
print("exact_agreement_unaliased\t%d" % exact_un)
print("exact_agreement_unaliased_rate\t%.4f" % (exact_un / len(both) if both else 0))
compat = sum(1 for s in both if compatible(nck[s], pgk[s]))
rate_c = compat / len(both) if both else 0.0
print("hierarchy_compatible\t%d" % compat)
print("hierarchy_compatible_rate\t%.4f" % rate_c)

for s in [x for x in both if not compatible(nck[x], pgk[x])][:8]:
    print("disagree\t%-28s nextclade=%-12s pangolin=%-12s (unaliased: %s vs %s)"
          % (s[:28], nck[s], pgk[s], unalias(nck[s]), unalias(pgk[s])))

# The floor is on the HIERARCHY-COMPATIBLE rate, because that is the quantity that means "the
# two callers placed this genome in the same part of the Pango tree". 0.80 is well below what
# two maintained callers on a curated example set should achieve and well above what a broken
# one would reach; the exact rate is reported, not asserted, since granularity differences are
# a real and legitimate difference between the methods.
if rate_c < 0.80:
    sys.exit("FAIL: hierarchy-compatible agreement %.4f is below the 0.80 floor" % rate_c)
print("crosscheck\tNextclade and pangolin place the same genomes compatibly in the Pango tree")

with open("score.tsv", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("observable\tvalue\n")
    fh.write("shared_sequences\t%d\n" % len(shared))
    fh.write("both_assigned\t%d\n" % len(both))
    fh.write("exact_agreement\t%d\n" % exact)
    fh.write("exact_agreement_rate\t%.4f\n" % (exact / len(both) if both else 0))
    fh.write("hierarchy_compatible\t%d\n" % compat)
    fh.write("exact_agreement_unaliased\t%d\n" % exact_un)
    fh.write("hierarchy_compatible_rate\t%.4f\n" % rate_c)
print("LINEAGE CROSSCHECK OK")
PYEOF
test "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: the comparison failed"; exit 1; }
cp score.tsv lineage-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "DONE"
